nodes.summary: If $L$ and $M$ are context-free languages over the same alphabet, then their union $L \cup M$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Closure of context-free languages under union

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ and a letter $a$, the number of $a$ is the position (counted from $0$) of the first occurrence of $a$ in the list of terminals occurring in the productions of $g$, or the length of that list when $a$ does not occur in it.
nodes.title: Letter numbering for the substitution grammar

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ and a natural number $k$, the letter with number $k$ is the entry at position $k$ (counted from $0$) of the list of terminals occurring in the productions of $g$; there is no such letter when $k$ is at least the length of that list.
nodes.title: Letter decoding for the substitution grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T$ with nonterminals $N_g$ and start symbol $S$, and let $e$ assign to each letter $a \in T$ an encoded grammar $e(a)$ over $T'$. The substitution grammar is the context-free grammar over $T'$ with nonterminals $N_g \sqcup (\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N})$, start symbol $S$ taken in the left part, and the productions of the substitution grammar for $g$ and $e$.
nodes.title: The substitution grammar

nodes.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be alphabets, $L$ a context-free language over $T$, and $\varphi$ a map sending each letter of $T$ to a word over $T'$. Then the language of all words $\varphi(a_1) \cdots \varphi(a_n)$ with $a_1 \cdots a_n \in L$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are closed under homomorphic images

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a context-free language over an alphabet $T$ and $M$ is a deterministic finite automaton over $T$ with finitely many states, then the intersection of $L$ with the language accepted by $M$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Intersection of a context-free language with the language of a DFA

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a context-free language and $R$ a regular language over the same alphabet, then $L \cap R$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Intersection of a context-free language with a regular language

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a context-free language, then its Kleene star $L^*$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Closure of context-free languages under Kleene star

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T$ with nonterminals $N_g$, and let $e$ assign to each letter $a \in T$ an encoded grammar $e(a)$ over $T'$. A production $A \to \alpha$ over $T$ with nonterminals in $N_g$ gives the production $A \to \alpha'$ over $T'$ with nonterminals in $N_g \sqcup (\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N})$, where $A$ is taken in the left part and $\alpha'$ is obtained from $\alpha$ by replacing…
nodes.title: Main production of the substitution grammar

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a context-free language over an alphabet $T$ and let $f \colon T \to T'$ be a map of alphabets. Then the image of $L$ under $f$, the language $\{f(a_1) \cdots f(a_n) \mid a_1 \cdots a_n \in L\}$ over $T'$, is context-free.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are closed under letter maps

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and let the sentential form $u$ derive $v$ in $g$ in zero or more steps. If every terminal occurring in $u$ occurs in some production of $g$, then every terminal occurring in $v$ occurs in some production of $g$.
nodes.title: Derivations keep the terminals among those of the grammar

nodes.summary: If $L$ and $M$ are context-free languages over the same alphabet, then their concatenation $LM = \{uv : u \in L,\ v \in M\}$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Closure of context-free languages under concatenation

nodes.summary: Every finite language is context-free.
nodes.title: Finite languages are context-free

nodes.summary: Over a finite alphabet, if $n$ is a natural number and every word of a language $L$ has length at most $n$, then $L$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Languages of bounded word length are context-free

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a context-free language, then for every natural number $n$ the power $L^n$, the concatenation of $n$ copies of $L$ (with $L^0$ the language containing only the empty word), is context-free.
nodes.title: Powers of a context-free language are context-free

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T$, and let $e$ assign to each letter $a \in T$ an encoded grammar $e(a)$ over $T'$. The productions of the substitution grammar are the main productions obtained from the productions of $g$, together with, for each terminal $a$ occurring in a production of $g$, the letter productions for $a$ obtained from the productions of $e(a)$.
nodes.title: Productions of the substitution grammar

nodes.title: Letter productions of the substitution grammar

nodes.title: Substituting the symbols of a grammar

nodes.summary: Context-free languages are closed under substitution by context-free languages.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are closed under substitution by context-free languages

Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
